sections.heading: How to structure and evaluate a test
sections.content: On Meta, start with one audience at the ad-set level and two nearly identical creatives that differ in just one variable, such as copy or image. Keep targeting conditions similar so you can isolate the change. Because the ad platform may deliver different impression counts to each creative, use a leveling metric—Becker gives click-through rate and impressions until conversion as examples—to compare efficiency fairly. Success criteria can be subjective, so use the results to identify what works for a particular audience or funnel stage.

sections.heading: Iterate, and use the platform's tools
sections.content: Send test learnings back to the creative team; for example, if one copy variation converts more frequently at a given funnel stage, use it as the base and test it against another variation. answer.summary: Becker recommended controlled, one-variable-at-a-time creative tests, comparing performance with suitable efficiency metrics when ad delivery is uneven. Most testing can be done in-platform; a specialized tool is not required. [S1, S2, S3]

sections.heading: How to set up and evaluate a test
sections.content: On Meta, use a single audience at the ad-set level and run two nearly identical creatives, changing just one variable—such as copy or an image—to isolate the effect. Keep targeting and other conditions similar. Because the platform may deliver different impression counts to each ad, compare efficiency with measures such as click-through rate or impressions until conversion, rather than relying only on raw totals. Which measure defines success is subjective; use the results to identify what works for a particular audience or funnel stage and share those learnings with the creative team. Then use the better-performing copy as a base and test another variation against it. [S1, S2, S4, S5]

sections.heading: Whether a specialized tool is needed
sections.content: No exotic or specialized tool is necessary for sophisticated creative testing. Becker said most of Thrive’s testing is done within the ad channels themselves, such as Meta Ads and Google Ads, and suggested using the testing structure above as a starting point. [S3]
